# fivenines_incidents (Data Source)

Lists incidents in the organization. All arguments are server-side filters; omitting them lists every incident.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Every argument is a server-side filter — omit them all to list everything.
data "fivenines_incidents" "all" {}

# Open incidents for one host, oldest first.
data "fivenines_incidents" "host_open" {
  host_id   = fivenines_instance.web.id
  status    = "open"
  direction = "asc"
}

# Incidents whose ACTIVE WINDOW overlaps last week. `to` is exclusive, so the
# range is [from, to) — and an incident that opened before `from` and is still
# open matches, because this is the incident's duration, not its creation time.
data "fivenines_incidents" "last_week" {
  from = "2026-08-24T00:00:00Z"
  to   = "2026-08-31T00:00:00Z"
}

output "open_incidents" {
  value = [for inc in data.fivenines_incidents.host_open.incidents : inc.title]
}

# Which incidents are visible on the organization's status pages.
output "published_incidents" {
  value = [for inc in data.fivenines_incidents.all.incidents : inc.title if inc.public]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Optional

- `direction` (String) Sort direction, `asc` or `desc`. Defaults to `desc`.
- `from` (String) Only incidents whose active window reaches this ISO 8601 time or later. This is the incident's duration, not its creation time: an incident that opened last week and is still open matches a `from` of yesterday.
- `host_id` (String) Only incidents affecting this instance (UUID).
- `order` (String) Sort column: `created_at`, `updated_at` or `title`. Defaults to `created_at`.
- `q` (String) Case-insensitive substring match on the incident title.
- `status` (String) Only incidents with this status. One of `unknown`, `warning`, `resolved`, `open`, `muted`, `acknowledged`.
- `task_id` (String) Only incidents affecting this task (UUID).
- `to` (String) Exclusive upper bound of the active window (ISO 8601). Combined with `from` the window is the half-open range `[from, to)`, so an incident starting exactly at `to` does not match and `from == to` matches nothing. An inverted window is an API error, not an empty list.
- `updated_since` (String) Only incidents whose `updated_at` is at or after this ISO 8601 timestamp (inclusive).
- `uptime_monitor_id` (String) Only incidents affecting this uptime monitor (UUID).
- `workflow_id` (Number) Only incidents raised by this workflow.

### Read-Only

- `incidents` (Attributes List) List of incidents. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--incidents))

<a id="nestedatt--incidents"></a>
### Nested Schema for `incidents`

Read-Only:

- `created_at` (String) Creation timestamp.
- `duration_seconds` (Number) Duration of the incident in whole seconds. For an open incident this is the elapsed time so far.
- `ended_at` (String) When the incident ended.
- `host_id` (String) Associated host ID.
- `id` (String) Unique identifier.
- `public` (Boolean) Whether the incident is shown on the organization's public status pages.
- `started_at` (String) When the incident started.
- `status` (String) Current status (unknown, warning, resolved, open, muted, acknowledged).
- `summary` (String) Incident summary.
- `task_id` (String) Associated task ID.
- `title` (String) Incident title.
- `updated_at` (String) Last update timestamp.
- `uptime_monitor_id` (String) Associated uptime monitor ID.
- `workflow_id` (String) Workflow that created this incident.
